text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leader of one of Nigeria's five political parties says military ruler General Sani Abacha is as free as any other Nigerian to contest for presidency in next year's election.
- Sack of money apparently dumped by armed robbers found in refuse dump near a school in Lagos, students say.
- Campaigning goes into full swing for next Saturday's local council polls.
- Military administrators of northern states say they are set for African trade fair scheduled for Kaduna, in the north, for one week at the end of March.
- Nigeria, Sierra Leone sign military training pact.

- As indications point that military ruler General Sani Abacha may contest next year's presidential election, presidential aspirants are rethinking their ambitions and opting to contest for seats in the national assembly instead.

- Military administrators of the 19 northern states resolve to contribute 100 million naira in order to raise the capital base of Bank of the North owned by their states to 500 million naira as directed by the regulatory authorities.
